      .where(and(eq(tasks.id, id), eq(tasks.userId, userId)))

      G. Complete Code Flow

      Registration, logout and session expiry flows are in Chapter 20 (Flows A–E).

      H. Testing

      WhatHowExpectedActualResult
      Typespnpm typecheckno errorsno errorsPassed
      Unit + integration testspnpm testall pass70 passed in 6 files (was 39; 30 new auth/authorization tests + 1 CSRF test)Passed
      Browser smoke testpnpm test:e2eall steps, no console errors18/18 passed, no console errorsPassed
      Upgrade of an existing databaseCopied the real data/todo.db (6 tasks from Entry #1), started the server on the copy, registered the first account in a real browserMigration runs; first account sees the 6 old tasks; API without cookie → 401Migration applied; 6 tasks visible; 401 UNAUTHORIZED without cookiePassed
      Visual checkScreenshots of the login screen and the logged-in appClean layout, name + admin badge + Users + Log outAs expectedPassed
      Documentationpnpm docs:buildHTML + PDF regenerated and verifiedSee the CHANGELOG entryPassed

      Issues found and handled during this work:

      • drizzle-kit generated ALTER TABLE … ADD user_id … REFERENCES users(id) without ON DELETE cascade. The not-yet-applied migration was corrected by hand (explained in Chapter 7).
      • Hono's csrf() treats requests with no Content-Type like form submissions. Body-less requests (complete, reopen, delete, logout) therefore need an Origin header — browsers always send it; the test helper now does too, and Chapter 5's curl examples were updated.
      • All test files switched to await createTestApp() because registering the default test user is asynchronous (password hashing).

      I. What I Learned

      • Authentication answers who are you?; authorization answers what may you do?
      • Passwords are stored only as salted, deliberately slow hashes.
      • A session is a random token in a cookie; the server keeps (a hash of) it in a table; logout deletes it.
      • Cookie flags (HttpOnly, SameSite, Secure) each stop a specific attack.
      • Authorization belongs in a place where it cannot be forgotten — here, every service query.
      • Returning 404 for other people's data hides that it exists.
      • Hiding a button in the UI is never a security measure; the server must check.

      J. What I Can Try Next

      1. Add PATCH /api/auth/password to change your password (verify the old one, hash the new one, delete your other sessions), with tests.
      2. Add PATCH /api/admin/users/:id so an admin can promote another user to admin — protected by requireRole('admin').
      3. Write a test proving that a deleted user's sessions stop working (hint: delete the row from users and rely on ON DELETE CASCADE).

      K. Important Notes

      • Register your own account first on any new installation: the first account becomes the admin.
      • Set COOKIE_SECURE=true whenever the site runs on HTTPS (always in production). On plain http://localhost keep it false, or the browser will refuse to store the cookie.
      • The seeded demo account (demo@example.com / demo-password-123) is for learning only — delete it before going live.
      • No password reset yet. The login throttle is in memory.
      • Older ownerless tasks are invisible until the first account registers and claims them.

      Development Entry: #4 — Question: What Is the Admin's ID and Password?

      Date: 2026-11-01

      A. What I Asked For

      "is the id password of admin" — which email (ID) and password log in as the administrator?

      B. What We Are Building

      No code change: an answer, a checked fact about the real database, and a new section in Chapter 20 ("What is the admin's email and password?") plus a Chapter 15 troubleshooting row.

      C. Why We Need It

      After Entry #3 the app requires a login, so you need to know how to get the first (admin) login.

      D. Technical Concepts

      • No default credentials: a password written in the source code is a security hole, because everyone with the code knows it.
      • First account = admin: set inside the registration transaction (Chapter 20).
      • Hashes cannot be reversed: a forgotten password cannot be "looked up", only replaced.

      E. Files Changed

      FileChange
      docs/DOCUMENTATION-SOURCE.mdNew Chapter 20 subsection, new Chapter 15 row, this entry
      docs/CHANGELOG.mdEntry #4
      docs/LEARN-HONO-COMPLETE.html, .pdfRegenerated

      F. Code Explanation

      The rule lives in registerUser (src/services/auth.service.ts):

      ts
      const isFirstUser = tx.select({ value: count() }).from(users).get()!.value === 0;
// ...
role: isFirstUser ? 'admin' : 'user',

      It counts the users inside the transaction; zero means this new account is the first one and gets the admin role.

      G. Complete Code Flow

      Development Entry: #5 — Bug Report: "Route POST /api/auth/register was not found."

      Date: 2026-11-01

      A. What I Asked For

      You reported that registering failed with the message "Route POST /api/auth/register was not found."

      B. What We Are Building

      No code change was needed. We found out why a route that exists in the code answered "not found", fixed the running environment, and added a troubleshooting entry so you can recognise this problem yourself.

      C. Why We Need It

      "The code is right but the app behaves as if it isn't" is one of the most common — and most confusing — problems in programming. Knowing the cause saves hours.

      D. Technical Concepts

      • A running program is a snapshot of the code. pnpm start reads the source files once. Editing files afterwards does not change the program that is already running; it must be restarted. (pnpm dev restarts automatically on every save.)
      • Process: a running program. Each has a process ID (PID). Only one process can listen on a port such as 3000.
      • The message came from our own notFoundHandler (src/middleware/error-handler.ts): "Route ${method} ${path} was not found." So the request did reach a Hono app — just one without the new route.

      E. Files Changed

      FileChange
      docs/DOCUMENTATION-SOURCE.mdChapter 15 troubleshooting row, this entry
      docs/CHANGELOG.mdEntry #5
      docs/LEARN-HONO-COMPLETE.html, .pdfRegenerated

      F. Code Explanation

      The route exists — it is registered in src/app.ts and src/routes/auth.routes.ts:

      ts
      app.route('/api/auth', authRoutes);                                          // src/app.ts
authRoutes.post('/register', validate('json', registerSchema), async (c) => { … });  // auth.routes.ts

      A Hono app only knows the routes that existed when the process started. The process on port 3000 had started before these lines were written.

      G. Complete Code Flow

      H. Testing

      CauseThat process was a server started by Claude during the initial build for screenshots; an earlier stop command did not end itConfirmed
      FixStopped the old processes (PIDs 24356, 37224) and started pnpm start with the current codeServer running
      Route exists nowPOST /api/auth/register with an empty body (so no account is created)400 VALIDATION_ERROR instead of 404 — the route exists
      Database upgradedRead data/todo.dbusers and sessions tables created by migration 0001
      Your registrationServer log + databasePOST /api/auth/register -> 201; account Minal Poudel (admin@gmail.com) is admin and owns all 6 earlier tasks; GET /api/admin/users -> 200

      I. What I Learned

      If the app behaves like an older version of the code, suspect an old process before suspecting the code. Check what is running and when it started, and restart.

      J. What I Can Try Next

      Run pnpm dev instead of pnpm start while changing code. Edit the text of a message in src/routes/auth.routes.ts, save, and watch the server restart by itself in the terminal.

      Only one program can use port 3000. If a fresh pnpm start fails with EADDRINUSE, an old copy is still running — see Chapter 15.

      Development Entry: #6 — Admin Assigns Tasks, Group & Individual Tasks, Subtasks, Separate Dashboard and Calendar Views, "Created By" for Admins

      Date: 2026-11-01

      A. What I Asked For

      "add a feature in admin to give a task to user and separate a dashboard and calendar like view too. add group task and individual task too, add a option to add task inside task, add a view to only admin on who created a task" — five features:

      1. Administrators can give (assign) tasks to users.
      2. A separate dashboard view and a calendar view.
      3. Group tasks and individual tasks.
      4. Tasks inside tasks.
      5. A view, for administrators only, showing who created each task.

      B. What We Are Building

      • Assignments: a task_assignees link table; admins pick one person (individual) or several (group) when creating or editing a task.
      • Group tasks: every member sees the same task, can edit, complete/reopen it and use its subtasks; only the creator or an admin can delete it; only admins change members.
      • Subtasks: a checklist inside every task (subtasks table, three new endpoints).
      • Views: Dashboard, Tasks, Calendar (month grid) and Admin tabs, switched with the URL hash.
      • Created by: tasks.created_by, sent to administrators only; shown on task cards and in the Admin view's All-tasks table.
      • Decisions made where the request left room (explained in Chapter 21): normal users keep creating individual tasks for themselves; subtasks are checklist items rather than full tasks; categories stay personal.

      C. Why We Need It

      The app becomes useful for a small team: an administrator can hand out and track work, people can share tasks, big tasks can be broken into steps, and deadlines are easy to see on a calendar.

      D. Technical Concepts

      All explained in Chapter 21 (and Chapter 7 for the migration): many-to-many relationships and link tables; composite primary keys; subqueries and IN (SELECT …); calculated vs stored values (isGroup); the N+1 query problem; booleans in SQLite; data migrations (INSERT INTO … SELECT); table rebuilds and why DROP TABLE can cascade; PRAGMA foreign_keys inside transactions; PRAGMA foreign_key_check; regression tests; hash routing; modulo arithmetic for calendars.

      Other issues found and fixed during the work:

      • drizzle-kit cannot ask its "is this a rename?" question in a non-interactive shell, so the change was split into two migrations (Chapter 7).
      • drizzle-kit again omitted the ON DELETE rule on an ALTER TABLE … ADD foreign key; added by hand.
      • The new server could not start at first because a leftover server process from earlier still held its log file; the leftover processes were stopped.
      • One smoke-test step clicked a tab before the login request had finished; the test now waits for the app to appear.

      I. What I Learned

      • A many-to-many relationship needs a link table; "is this a group?" is best calculated from it.
      • Authorization can depend on the role (viewer.role) as well as on ownership, and different actions (see / edit / delete / assign) can have different rules.
      • Sending a field only to some users (createdBy) is another form of authorization.
      • Load related data for many rows at once to avoid the N+1 problem.
      • Migrations that move data need extra care: test them on a copy of real data, back up first, and add a regression test.

      • Tasks without a due date do not appear in the calendar.

      Development Entry: #7 — Different View Types in the Calendar

      Date: 2026-11-01

      A. What I Asked For

      "add different view type in calendar" — besides the month grid, other ways of looking at the calendar.

      B. What We Are Building

      A Month / Week / Day / Agenda switcher above the calendar (details in Chapter 21, "The calendar's four view types"). ‹ › move by the size of the current view, Today jumps back, clicking a date opens it in the Day view, and the chosen view type is remembered in the browser.

      C. Why We Need It

      Different questions need different views: the month for the big picture, the week for planning, the day for focus, and the agenda for "what's coming next?" without empty days.

      D. Technical Concepts

      • View state as data: a mode plus an anchor date describe any calendar view.
      • Pure functions (calendarRange, shiftCalendar): output depends only on input — easy to reason about.
      • Date arithmetic with getDay(), modulo (% 7) and JavaScript's automatic month roll-over.
      • localStorage for remembering a harmless preference, and why it is unsuitable for secrets.
      • aria-pressed on toggle buttons, so screen readers announce which view is active.
      • CSS modifier classes (mode-week, mode-day, …) switching a grid layout to a list layout, and a media query turning the week into a vertical list on phones.

      Development Entry: #9 — How to Host on cPanel

      Date: 2026-11-03

      A. What I Asked For

      "add a how to host in cPanel" — instructions for putting the app online on cPanel shared hosting.

      B. What We Are Building

      • server.cjs, a startup file that cPanel's Setup Node.js App (Phusion Passenger) can run.
      • Chapter 22 — Hosting on cPanel: requirements, how Passenger runs the app, five steps (domain + HTTPS, code via Git deploy key or ZIP, creating the Node.js app with environment variables, installing with pnpm, starting and testing), updating, backups, troubleshooting and the limits of shared hosting.

      C. Why We Need It

      cPanel is the most common kind of affordable hosting. Without a startup file Passenger cannot start a TypeScript app, and a few cPanel details (the "Run NPM Install" button, where to keep the database, COOKIE_SECURE) easily go wrong.

      D. Technical Concepts

      Phusion Passenger and application startup files; CommonJS vs ES modules and why the starter is a .cjs file; dynamic import(); tsx's register() API; SSH deploy keys; environment variables in a hosting panel; keeping data outside the app and public folders; restarting with tmp/restart.txt.

      E. Files Changed

      FileChange
      server.cjsNew — Passenger/cPanel startup file
      README.mdNew "Hosting" section
      docs/DOCUMENTATION-SOURCE.mdNew Chapter 22; Preface table, Chapter 9 tree, Chapter 11 configuration table and Chapter 17 point to it; glossary; this entry
      docs/CHANGELOG.mdEntry #9

      No application code changed.

      F. Code Explanation

      server.cjs is explained line by line in Chapter 22 ("Why server.cjs?"): require('tsx/esm/api') + register() teach Node.js to run TypeScript, and import('./src/index.ts') starts the same code as pnpm start. Passenger takes over the server's listen() call, so src/index.ts did not need to change.

      G. Complete Code Flow

      H. Testing

      Existing testspnpm typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm test:e2eunchangedno errors; 93/93; 26/26, no console errorsPassed
      Real cPanel server——Not tested (no access to your hosting account); Chapter 22 says so—

      I. What I Learned

      How shared hosting runs Node.js apps (Passenger + a startup file), why the starter must be CommonJS, how a deploy key gives a server read-only access to a private repository, and why the database belongs outside the app and public folders.

      J. What I Can Try Next

      1. Deploy to a test subdomain following Chapter 22, then practise an update with git pull and touch tmp/restart.txt.
      2. Write a small shell script deploy.sh that runs the three update commands.
      3. Set up a cron job in cPanel that makes a daily database backup.

      K. Important Notes

      • Use the Terminal + pnpm, not the "Run NPM Install" button.
      • Set COOKIE_SECURE=true and use HTTPS; register your own admin account first.
      • Keep DATABASE_PATH outside public_html, the domain's document root and the app folder.

      Development Entry: #10 — Use the Real Aeto Logo, and How to Host on Render

      Date: 2026-11-03

      A. What I Asked For

      "change into this logo and add how to render in (render)" — with the light (cream and orange) Aeto logo attached: show this logo in the app, and explain how to host the app on Render.

      B. What We Are Building

      • The real logo replaces the hand-drawn swoosh: in the top bar, above the login card, and on the manual's cover.
      • render.yaml, a Render Blueprint, and Chapter 23 — Hosting on Render (the persistent-disk rule, the Blueprint line by line, step-by-step setup, updates, backups, troubleshooting, and a cPanel-vs-Render comparison).

      C. Why We Need It

      The app should carry the actual brand, not an approximation. Render is the easiest way to run the app from GitHub with automatic HTTPS and automatic deploys — but SQLite needs a persistent disk there, which is easy to get wrong.

      D. Technical Concepts

      Transparent PNGs and cropping; <img> width/height and layout shift; data URLs (embedding an image in HTML as base64 text); CSS specificity (why .logo span beat .logo-product); Platform-as-a-Service; ephemeral filesystems and persistent disks; Blueprints (infrastructure described in a file); health checks; auto-deploy on push.

      E. Files Changed

      FileChange
      public/img/aeto-logo-light.pngNew — the logo, cropped from 1000 × 1000 to 928 × 342
      public/img/aeto-mark.svgDeleted — replaced by the real logo
      public/index.htmlLogo image in the top bar and on the login screen
      public/css/styles.css.logo-img, .logo .logo-product, .auth-brand, login screen layout
      scripts/build-docs.tsLogo embedded as a data URL on the manual's cover
      render.yamlNew — Render Blueprint
      server.cjsComment: also the Render start file
      README.md, docs/*Hosting section, Chapters 8, 9, 11, 17, new Chapter 23, this entry

      F. Code Explanation

      • The crop was done with a browser canvas: find the bounding box of all non-transparent pixels, add 8 px, and copy that rectangle into a new PNG.
      • scripts/build-docs.ts reads the PNG and writes data:image/png;base64,… into the cover's <img src>, so the HTML manual still works offline as a single file.
      • In the top bar, .logo span { color: var(--primary) } (one class + one element) was more specific than .logo-product (one class), so "To-Do" first appeared in the darker button orange; the rule is now .logo .logo-product (two classes), which wins.
      • render.yaml is explained line by line in Chapter 23.

      G. Complete Code Flow

      I. What I Learned

      How to prepare a logo for the web (crop, transparency, explicit size), how to embed an image in a standalone HTML file, why CSS specificity decides which rule wins, and why a cloud platform's disk is temporary unless you add a persistent one.

      J. What I Can Try Next

      K. Important Notes

      • Render's free instance has no persistent disk: data would be lost on every deploy. Use a paid instance with the disk from render.yaml.

      Glossary

      TermMeaning
      AdminA user with the admin role; may use /api/admin/*
      APIApplication Programming Interface — URLs a program can call to read or change data
      Arrow functionShort function syntax: (x) => x * 2
      AssigneeA person a task is assigned to (a row in task_assignees)
      async / awaitKeywords for writing code that waits for Promises step by step
      AuthenticationChecking who someone is (login); failure → 401
      AuthorizationChecking what someone may do (own data, roles); failure → 403 or 404
      Blueprint (Render)A render.yaml file in the repository that describes services, so Render can create them automatically
      Brute-force attackTrying many passwords until one works; slowed down by the login throttle
      BackendThe part of an application that runs on the server
      Body (HTTP)The data part of a request or response, e.g. JSON
      Build idA fingerprint printed on both manual formats to show they come from the same source
      CallbackA function passed to another function to be called later
      CloneDownload a Git repository (with its history) for the first time
      cPanelA web-hosting control panel used by many shared-hosting companies
      ColumnOne named piece of information in a database table
      CommitA saved snapshot of the project in Git, with a message explaining the change
      Contrast ratioHow different text and background colours are in brightness; at least 4.5 : 1 for normal text (WCAG AA)
      Composite primary keyA primary key made of several columns together, e.g. (task_id, user_id)
      Constant-time comparisonComparing secrets in a way that always takes the same time (timingSafeEqual)
      Context (c)Hono's per-request object with the request, response helpers and stored variables
      CookieA small named value the browser stores for a site and sends back with every request to it
      CRUDCreate, Read, Update, Delete
      CSPContent Security Policy — a header limiting where a page may load scripts and styles from
      CSRFCross-Site Request Forgery — another website making your browser send requests to our app with your cookie
      CSSThe language that styles web pages
      Data URLAn image (or other file) written directly into HTML/CSS as text, e.g. data:image/png;base64,…
      DebounceWaiting until a burst of events stops before reacting (used for search)
      DependencyA package your project needs
      Deploy keyAn SSH key that gives one server read access to one GitHub repository
      Dynamic importimport('./file') used as a function at run time; works even in CommonJS files
      Dependency injectionGiving code the things it needs (like the database) instead of letting it fetch them itself
      DOMDocument Object Model — the browser's in-memory tree of the page
      Drizzle ORMThe TypeScript library we use to query the database
      EndpointOne method + URL combination of an API, e.g. POST /api/tasks
      Ephemeral filesystemStorage that is wiped when a cloud service restarts or redeploys
      Environment variableA named setting given to a program by the operating system, e.g. PORT
      Event listenerA function that runs when an event (click, submit…) happens
      fetchThe browser function for sending HTTP requests
      Foreign keyA column that refers to the primary key of another table
      FrontendThe part of an application that runs in the browser
      GitA version control system that records the history of a project's files
      GitHubA website that hosts Git repositories online
      GenericA type with a placeholder filled in later, e.g. Array<string>
      HandlerThe function that runs when a route matches
      Group taskA task assigned to two or more people, who share it
      HashA one-way "fingerprint" of data; used for passwords (scrypt) and session tokens (SHA-256)
      Hash (URL) / hash routingThe part of an address after #; changing it switches views without reloading the page
      Header (HTTP)A Name: value line with extra information about a request or response
      HonoThe web framework this project uses
      HttpOnlyA cookie flag that hides the cookie from page JavaScript
      IDORInsecure Direct Object Reference — reaching other people's records by changing an ID in the URL
      Individual taskA task assigned to exactly one person
      HTMLThe language describing the structure of web pages
      HTTPThe protocol browsers and servers use to communicate
      Index (database)A structure that makes searching a column faster
      Integration testA test that checks several parts working together
      JSONJavaScript Object Notation — a text format for data
      JWTJSON Web Token — a signed token containing user data; an alternative to database sessions
      LEFT JOINSQL that combines rows from two tables, keeping rows without a match
      localStorageA small key–value store in the browser that survives reloads; good for preferences, never for secrets
      Link table (join table)A table whose rows connect rows of two other tables, creating a many-to-many relationship
      Many-to-manyA relationship where each side can have many of the other (tasks ↔ users)
      LockfileA file recording exact package versions (pnpm-lock.yaml)
      MiddlewareCode that runs before/after route handlers
      MigrationA versioned file of SQL that changes the database structure
      ModuleA file that shares code with export and uses code with import
      N+1 query problemRunning one query for a list and then one more per item; avoided by loading related rows for all items at once
      Node.jsA program that runs JavaScript outside the browser
      npmThe public package registry, and Node's default package manager
      NULL"No value" in a database
      Persistent diskCloud storage that survives restarts and deploys (needed for SQLite on Render)
      Passenger (Phusion Passenger)The program cPanel uses to start Node.js apps and hand them web requests
      Parameterised querySQL where values are sent separately from the SQL text — prevents SQL injection
      pnpmThe fast, disk-efficient package manager this project uses
      PortA numbered "door" on a computer where a server listens (ours: 3000)
      Primary keyA column that uniquely identifies each row
      Pure functionA function whose result depends only on its inputs and that changes nothing else
      Push / remoteUpload commits to the online copy of a repository (the "remote", usually named origin)
      Regression testA test written for a bug, so the bug can never silently come back
      Repository (repo)A project folder whose history is tracked by Git
      PromiseAn object representing a value that will be available later
      Query parameterkey=value data after ? in a URL
      RESTA style of API design using resources (URLs) and HTTP methods
      RouteA method + path connected to a handler
      RoleA user's permission level: user or admin
      RowOne record in a database table
      SaltRandom bytes mixed into a password before hashing, so equal passwords get different hashes
      SameSiteA cookie flag controlling whether the cookie is sent with requests started by other websites
      scryptA deliberately slow, memory-hard password-hashing function built into Node.js
      Secure (cookie)A cookie flag: only send the cookie over HTTPS
      SessionA server-side record that a browser is logged in, identified by a random token in a cookie
      Schema (database)The description of all tables and columns
      Schema (Zod)A description of what valid data looks like
      ServiceA function in src/services containing business logic and database access
      SQLThe language for talking to relational databases
      SQL injectionAn attack that sneaks SQL commands into user input
      SQLiteA database stored in a single file
      Stack traceThe list of function calls leading to an error
      Static fileA file sent to the browser unchanged (HTML, CSS, JS, images)
      SubqueryA query inside another query, e.g. id IN (SELECT task_id FROM …)
      SubtaskA checklist item inside a task
      Status codeA three-digit number summarising an HTTP response (200, 404…)
      tsxA tool that runs TypeScript files directly in Node.js
      TransactionA group of database changes that are saved together or not at all
      TypeA description of what kind of value something is
      Type inferenceTypeScript working out a type automatically
      TypeScriptJavaScript with types
      Unit testA test that checks one small piece in isolation
      User enumerationFinding out which emails have accounts from differences in error messages or timing
      ValidationChecking that input data follows the rules
      ViewerIn our services: the logged-in user (id and role) on whose behalf data is read or changed
      VitestThe testing framework this project uses
      WALWrite-Ahead Log — a SQLite mode that writes changes to a side file first
      XSSCross-Site Scripting — an attack that injects code into a web page
      ZodThe library we use to validate data

      2026-11-01 — Entry #6: Admin assigns tasks, group and individual tasks, subtasks, separate views, "created by" for admins

      Original request: "add a feature in admin to give a task to user and sepraste a dash board and calander like view too / add group task and inviuwal task too add a option to add task inside task add a view to only aadmin on who created a task"

      Summary:

      • Assignments: a new task_assignees link table (many-to-many) replaces the single owner column tasks.user_id.
        • Admins assign a task to one person (individual) or several people (group).
        • Normal users keep creating individual tasks for themselves.
      • Group tasks: every member sees, edits and completes the same task and shares its checklist.
        • Only the creator or an admin can delete a group task.
        • Only admins change who it's assigned to.
      • Subtasks: a checklist inside every task, via a new subtasks table and the endpoints POST /api/tasks/:id/subtasks, PATCH /api/subtasks/:id and DELETE /api/subtasks/:id.
      • Views: Dashboard (7 cards including Group tasks, plus Overdue and Next-7-days lists), Tasks (with an Individual/Group filter), Calendar (month grid; "+" adds a task on that day) and Admin (users, plus all tasks with Type, Assigned to and Created by). They are switched with URL hash routing.
      • "Created by": a new tasks.created_by column. The creator is included in API responses for admins only; normal users get canDelete instead.
      • New API features: GET /api/admin/tasks, the assigneeIds field on create and update, the kind, dueFrom and dueTo filters, and groupTasks on the dashboard.
      • Data-loss bug found and fixed before it reached real data:
        • The table rebuild in migration 0003 cascade-deleted all assignee rows, because Drizzle runs migrations inside a transaction, where SQLite ignores PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF.
        • runMigrations now turns foreign keys off outside the transaction, runs PRAGMA foreign_key_check, and turns them back on. A regression test was added for this.
      • Real database: backed up to data/backups/todo-before-assignees-2026-11-01.db, then migrated. All 7 tasks kept their creator and assignee.

      2026-11-01 — Entry #3: Authentication and authorization

      Original request: "add ahotrizastion and authetication and add it in doc too" (add authorization and authentication, and document them)

      Summary:

      • Accounts: register, log in, log out and /api/auth/me.
        • Passwords are stored as salted scrypt hashes (Node's built-in crypto, so no new dependencies).
      • Sessions:
        • A 32-byte random token is kept in an HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie (with Secure when COOKIE_SECURE=true).
        • Only the token's SHA-256 hash is stored, in a new sessions table.
        • Sessions last 7 days, and logout deletes them.
      • Authentication: requireAuth protects every task, category, dashboard and admin route (401 without a valid session).
      • Authorization:
        • Tasks and categories have an owner (user_id), and every service query filters by the logged-in user. Other users' records answer 404.
        • Category names are unique per user.
        • requireRole('admin') protects GET /api/admin/users (403 for other users).
        • The first account becomes admin and claims all existing ownerless data.
      • Hardening:
        • Hono csrf() middleware.
        • Login throttling: 5 failures per email within 15 minutes gives 429.
        • The same error message, and similar timing, for an unknown email and a wrong password.
      • Frontend:
        • Login/register screen, plus the signed-in user's name, an admin badge and a Log out button.
        • An admin-only Users dialog.
        • Automatic return to the login screen after a 401.
      • Seed script: now creates the demo account demo@example.com / demo-password-123.

      Files created:

      • Migration: src/db/migrations/0001_add_users_and_sessions.sql, src/db/migrations/meta/0001_snapshot.json

      2026-11-01 — Entry #2: Install the project with pnpm

      Original request: "install it through pnpm"

      Summary: Switched the project from npm to pnpm. Removed npm's lockfile and node_modules, reinstalled every package with pnpm, and added pnpm-workspace.yaml. The first install failed because pnpm tried to compile better-sqlite3 from C++ source with node-gyp, and this computer has no C++ build tools. The package already ships prebuilt binaries, so it is now set to allowBuilds: false; esbuild stays allowed. package.json was cleaned up: removed npm's allowScripts, added packageManager, moved tsx to dependencies, removed the unused build/start:prod scripts and the dotenv package (Node's built-in process.loadEnvFile is used instead), and set engines.node to >=22.

      2026-11-01 — Entry #1: Initial build of the Hono To-Do application and learning manual

      Original request: Build a fully functional Hono To-Do application (Hono, TypeScript, Node.js, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, Zod, HTML/CSS/vanilla JavaScript, Vitest). It needs a dashboard, full task management, categories, search, filters and sorting, plus a professional interface with notifications and loading, error and empty states. Also create a complete beginner-friendly learning manual in HTML and PDF, generated from a Markdown source with docs:build, and keep a changelog.

      Summary:

      • Backend:
        • Hono app built in layers: routes → Zod validation → services → Drizzle/SQLite.
        • Central error handling.
        • Request-logging, security-header, body-limit and database-injection middleware.
      • API: 13 endpoints covering health, tasks (list, get, create, edit, complete, reopen, delete), categories (list, create, edit, delete) and the dashboard.
      • Database: tasks and categories tables with a foreign key (ON DELETE SET NULL), indexes, and a generated migration 0000_init.sql.
      • Frontend: a responsive single page with a dashboard, filters, a task list, create/edit and category dialogs, a confirmation dialog, toasts, and loading/error/empty states. It is XSS-safe because it renders with textContent.
      • Tests: 39 Vitest tests and an 11-step browser smoke test.
      • Scripts: migrate, seed, e2e smoke test, documentation generator.
      • Manual: 19 chapters, a Development Log, a Glossary, and this change history.
